data.text/markdown:
Classic signals · tuning

This notebook finds settings for the strategy of classic_signals_marimo.py for one stock at a time (pick it in section 1), checks whether they hold up, and exports them, so that notebook can start from them.
  1. The data: pick the stock to tune; its candles of the training window (Jan 2025 – Jun 2026) and of the validation window (Jul 2026 – 16 Oct 2026). Everything from 17 Oct 2026 on is the final check: never loaded here
  2. The search space: what the optimizer may choose. By default it decides everything itself (every rule's switch on or off, every number in its range); you only override what you want fixed
  3. The objective: the daily Sharpe ratio on the training window, the luck line it must clear, and the validation score recorded beside it
  4. A quick check: one run with the optimizer's first trial
  5. The optimization: a new run, or more trials for an earlier one; watch it live in Optuna's dashboard
  6. Which hyperparameters matter: each one moved across its range, the rest held: what it does to the score, and which ones do nothing at all
  7. Does the procedure hold up? The walk forward inside the training window: the optimization repeated every few sessions, each block traded with settings chosen on earlier sessions only
  8. The export: the best settings for the stock, one complete set, as a file the main notebook loads under Starting values
The heavy steps (5, 6, 7) only run when you click their button.

1 · The data

Pick the stock to tune below: everything in this notebook (the quick check, the optimization, the effects, the walk forward and the export) then works on that stock alone. Changing it reloads its candles and starts over. Loaded: the stock's one-minute candles (every stored hour: the bands and the moving average may read the hours outside the regular session) and the daily candles of the stock, its sector fund and the market fund, for the training window (the optimizer chooses on it) and the validation window (every trial is also scored on it, to watch, never to choose). The months after the validation window are the final check and are never loaded here. The stock gets a lab: the strategy for any settings, its parts (candles, bands, trends, levels, ...) built once and kept, so trying many settings mostly reuses them.

data.text/markdown:
2 · The search space: what the optimizer may choose

By default the optimizer decides everything itself: every rule's switch (on or off), every number within its range, every choice. You only step in where you want a say:
  • a switch: optimizer decides, always on or always off
  • a number: the optimizer picks a value from … to, in steps of step. Set from and to to the same value to fix it there
  • a choice (candle size, stop, holding limit, profit target, ...): the values the optimizer may pick from. Leave just one to fix it
The grey text says what each one does and what a change rebuilds: a change of the candles or of an indicator makes a trial slower than a change of a rule or of the exit. A rule's lever only matters while its rule is on, a stop's distance only with its kind of stop, the percent target only with the percent target: a trial that leaves one out does not draw it. The starting ranges come from hyperparams.py (a lever's: from its rule's file in rules/): change them there to make a range the default for good, or here for this session. Reset puts every control back. Table 2 sums up the space as it stands. The optimizer's first trial uses the values of first trial: the built-in ones, or a stock's values from a file this notebook exported before. One hint from a first short run: free, the optimizer switched the earnings guard off for two stocks (only a handful of reports in the history, so it saw no reason to keep it), although on its own it raised NOW's score. Set it to always on if you want it kept.

data.text/html:
The rules: on or off

band fadeA close outside a band, then a close back inside: long when it comes back from below the lower band, short when it comes back from above the upper band. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
band breakoutThe close stays outside a band for a set number of candles in a row: long above the upper band, short below the lower band. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
moving averageThe minute chart's moving average: above a rising average allows longs only, below a falling one shorts only, a flat one both. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
stock trendThe stock's own daily trend at the previous close: up allows longs only, down shorts only, sideways both. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
sector trendThe sector fund's daily trend at the previous close: up allows longs only, down shorts only, sideways both. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
market trendThe market fund's (SPY) daily trend at the previous close: up allows longs only, down shorts only, sideways both. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
major levelsNo long just under a major level and no short just above one: the next level must leave some room (in typical moves). · a change rebuilds the decisions only
previous high / lowNo long just under the previous session's high or low, no short just above one: it must leave some room (in typical moves). · a change rebuilds the decisions only
wait after the openNo new trade in the first minutes after 09:30: a signal whose trade would fill in that time is dropped (open trades keep their stop). · a change rebuilds the decisions only
earnings guardNo new trade in the session(s) before a quarterly report moves the stock, and an open trade is closed at the close before it. · a change rebuilds the decisions only

The rules' levers

band breakout: closes in a row outside the bandA lever of 'band breakout': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
moving average: its rise is measured over, candlesA lever of 'moving average': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
moving average: flat zone, ± typical movesA lever of 'moving average': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
major levels: room needed to the next level, typical movesA lever of 'major levels': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
previous high / low: room needed, typical movesA lever of 'previous high / low': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
wait after the open: minutes after 09:30 without new tradesA lever of 'wait after the open': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only
earnings guard: sessions before a report without new tradesA lever of 'earnings guard': it only acts while that rule is on. · a change rebuilds the decisions only

The exit

the stopHow the stop is set: trailing the best price since the entry (by typical moves or by a percentage) or fixed at a percentage from the entry. · a change rebuilds how the trades end
trailing stop: typical moves behind the best priceHow far the trailing stop trails, in typical moves. · a change rebuilds how the trades end · only with stop_kind: moves
stop distance, % of the priceHow far the percent stop sits from the best price (trailing) or the entry (fixed). · a change rebuilds how the trades end · only with stop_kind: percent trailing / percent fixed
holding limitClose a trade at the end of its n-th session (1: never overnight). · a change rebuilds how the trades end
profit targetClose a trade at the next level in its direction (at least one typical move from the entry), or at a fixed percentage from the entry. · a change rebuilds how the trades end
profit target, % of the priceHow far the percent profit target sits from the entry. · a change rebuilds how the trades end · only with target_kind: percent

Candles and indicators

candle sizeThe candles the strategy trades and every intraday indicator reads. · a change rebuilds every candle and indicator
band: candles in the averageHow many candles the bands' middle line averages. Longer: slower bands. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
band distance, standard deviationsHow far the bands sit from the middle. Wider: rarer, more extreme signals. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
bands and average also read the hours outside the regular sessionWhether the bands and the moving average run through the pre-market, the after-hours and the night too (earlier, but jumpier). · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
moving average: candlesThe minute chart's moving average (read by the moving-average filter). · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
trend average, daysThe daily average the stock, sector and market trends compare the close with (read by the three daily trend filters, and the market condition of a trade). · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
its rise is measured over, daysOver how many days the trend average's rise is measured. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
flat zone, ± typical daily movesHow little the average may move and still count as flat (sideways). · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
turning point: highest/lowest of ± daysHow many days on each side a turning point must top (or undercut). · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
memory: sessions backHow old a turning point may be and still count. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
same level if closer than, × typical daily moveHow close turning points must be to form one level. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
turning points neededHow many turning points make a major level. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
a ceiling and a floor may form one levelWhether swing highs and swing lows group together. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
typical move: candle sizeThe candles the typical move (the stop's yardstick) is measured on. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it
typical move: candles averagedHow many of those candles the typical move averages. · a change rebuilds one indicator and the rules that read it

The optimizer chooses 38 of the 38 hyperparameters; 0 are fixed. Together they span about 10^33 combinations: far more than any tuning can try, so Optuna samples the promising part. 10 of them only count while a switch or a choice allows them, and 15 rebuild an indicator when they change (slower trials).

data.text/markdown:
3 · The objective

The score of a setting is its daily Sharpe ratio on the training window: the profit of every session after costs (an open trade valued at the session's last close), its average divided by how much it swings from session to session, scaled to a year (× √252). 1 means a year's profit about as large as a year's swings; 2 is what traders call very good. Fewer than the minimum trades per session and the setting has no score, so "never trade" cannot win. The profit, the trades and the worst drawdown are recorded beside it. Why this score: a test on 500 random settings of NOW (2025 against 2026 H1) found no score that picks settings that keep working better than another (profit ÷ worst drawdown, total profit, profitable months: all about alike). This one has two things the others lack. It does not grow with the window's length, so the training and the validation scores compare directly. And it has a known scale of luck: The luck line. Without any edge, the best of ||(n||) settings still reaches about ||(\Phi^{-1}(0.5^{1/n}) \times \sqrt{252 / \text{sessions}}||) by chance (Φ⁻¹: the inverse of the normal curve). Trying more settings raises the line: about 0.24 for 10 trials on 373 sessions, 0.42 for 100, 0.61 for 5,000. A best score that does not clearly clear it has found nothing. (Settings that resemble each other are not independent, so the true line is somewhat lower; on NOW it came out 0.1 lower.) The validation score: every trial is also scored on the validation window, beside the training score, never used to choose. Section 5 draws both: if the training score does not predict the validation score across trials, the optimizer is fitting noise.

4 · A quick check

One run of the stock with the optimizer's first trial (the first trial values, moved into the search space: a fixed hyperparameter at its value), on the training window and on the validation window, and how long it took (the first run builds the parts, later ones mostly reuse them). With the same values, the main notebook shows the same trades: both run pipeline.py.

data.text/markdown:
5 · The optimization

Optuna tries settings from the search space and keeps the one with the best training score. Each run first tries a few settings at random (a third of its trials, at most 10) before it models which ones score well. Figure 1 shows every trial: its training score, the best so far, the luck line and the validation score of the best so far; and every trial's training against its validation score. Table 4 compares, for every hyperparameter the optimizer chooses, the first trial's value with the best; Table 5 the scores. Runs are kept and can be continued. Every run is written, trial by trial, to one journal file under its name. To add trials later, pick the run under run (it continues with its own search space, first trial and minimum trades: sections 2 and 3 do not apply to it) and click the button again. A run whose inputs changed since (the data, the windows or the code) cannot be continued: start a new one. Watch a run live in Optuna's dashboard. Run this in a terminal and leave it running: uvx optuna-dashboard /Users/janmarti/Documents/code/stock-trading-simple/strategies/classic_signals/studies/tuning.log then open http://127.0.0.1:8080: the start page lists every run; click one. History draws each trial's score and the best so far, Hyperparameter Importance ranks the settings by how much they move the score, Slice plots each setting against the score, and Trials lists every trial with its settings, its profit and trades and its validation score. A trial with too few trades shows as pruned (no score). The pages update as trials finish.
Pick a run or name a new one, then click run the optimization (about a second per trial; the first one per indicator is slower).

6 · Which hyperparameters move the score?

Around one set of values (the best of the run if one ran, else the optimizer's first trial), every hyperparameter is moved across its range on its own, everything else held, and the strategy is scored on the training window. Table 6 ranks them by their effect: the highest score minus the lowest, among the values that traded enough to be scored; values trading too little counts the others (a sign the range reaches settings that hardly trade). An effect of 0 means the hyperparameter does nothing here, and the last column says why (it is not in use: its rule is off, or another stop or target kind is chosen; or no trade changed at all). Figure 2 draws the score against the value for the strongest ones (the black dot: the value as set; a red cross: a value that traded too little to be scored). This is a look around one point: a hyperparameter can matter more (or less) once others change. A best setting whose neighbours all score far lower is a lone spike: luck, most likely.
Click measure the effects (one run per value: about a minute).

data.text/markdown:
7 · Does the procedure hold up? The walk forward

The optimization, repeated every refit sessions from a first session on, inside the training window: each block of sessions traded with the settings chosen on the sessions before it, stitched into one record. Against it, no tuning (the optimizer's first trial throughout): the control the tuned walk must beat, on the same sessions. The candle size must be fixed in the search space for a walk (a walk trades one size). Figure 3 draws the profit curves, Table 7 the bottom line, Figure 4 the settings the walk chose over time (values that jump from one tuning to the next mean the tuning follows noise). The walks run in separate processes and are kept on disk (var/classic_signals/tuning/): a repeat with the same inputs is instant.
The walk forward trades one candle size: leave just one candle size in the search space (section 2; one walk per size).

8 · The export

Writes the best settings of the run (section 5) for the stock, one complete set of every hyperparameter, with what made them (the run, the search space, the scores, the data), to var/classic_signals/settings/<date>-<name>.json. In the main notebook, pick the file under Starting values: every control there then starts at these values, for further inspection by hand.
Run the optimization (section 5), then click export the best settings.
